rows.description: A junior watches a leader who admits mistakes, gives credit and asks for views. They learn that authority based on trust lasts longer than authority based on position.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A wise leader gives freedom to the experienced, guidance to the new and honest feedback to all. They ask what each person needs, not what suits their own habit.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Young children learn to build a block tower together and argue over who places what. Taking turns is fragile and needs adult help, but it is the seed of teamwork.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: Children choosing sides feel the sting of being picked last or the pride of being picked first. They also start to learn that a team needs different strengths.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child left until the end of team selection feels their worth measured in public. They may laugh it off, and a kind captain who picks them warmly can undo much of the hurt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: Teenagers on a team clash over who leads, who gets credit and whose idea wins. The fight is often about respect and recognition, not the task itself.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A team captain acknowledges each member's role in a win and takes a share of blame in a loss. This teaches the group that mistakes are safe to admit.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student sees a new project team go from polite to tense to workable. Understanding that early friction is normal keeps them from giving up too soon.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Trust broken by a missed deadline [Receiver]
rows.description: A team member is let down by a teammate who does not deliver and does not say so. The problem is less the delay than the silence, which makes future promises harder to believe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A team member holds back irritation for weeks, smiling in meetings, until a small trigger produces an outburst. Unspoken issues do not vanish, they gather force.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
